correctness.rationale: The source model requires positive C1 dispersal fractions whose column sums are strictly below 1; the explicit smoothstep is nondecreasing C1, has values in [1/20,1/2], and retention q-d remains in [3/10,3/4]. Exact f(1)=2 and f(3)=3 give F(1,3)=(3,1) and F(3,1)=(1,3). Both endpoint slopes vanish, yielding J13=[[3/4,1/8],[1/20,3/40]] and J31 its patch permutation, with M=J31 J13 and infinity norm 13/64<1, proving local attraction. The symmetric state u=11/5 has transverse multiplier -13891/8000<-1. For constant migration, positivity and monotonic recruitment give h(min)<=min-next<=max-next<=h(max), with h(z)=16z/[5(1+z)]; reciprocal iteration 1/h(z)=(5/16)(1/z+1) proves global convergence of nonzero states to u. Hyperbolicity/IFT proves C1 robustness. The packaged standard-library verifier reproduces all exact rational constants; finite test loops are not a proof of the universal claim.

originality.rationale: Relevant mathematical text in the initiating 2024 preprint defines the full C1 costly-dispersal class and numerically exhibits cycles in source-sink Ricker/Hassell settings; it does not derive the constructed identical monotone Beverton-Holt antiphase two-cycle or its exact stability certificate. The 2023 constant-dispersal Beverton-Holt analysis concerns equilibrium total biomass under constant coupling. A related 2018 active/refuge result reports global convergence for the Beverton-Holt case and period-two behavior in an Allee-effect regime, but only its abstract/contextual excerpts were accessible. Published mathematical-record searches did not identify a statement implying the exact constructed mechanism. Priority risk from unindexed work and unread full text remains explicitly acknowledged.

value.rationale: The 2024 initiating study numerically documents 2-cycles in a coupled Ricker/Hassell source-sink system, leaving open whether feedback alone, without an overcompensatory local population map, can generate antiphase cycling. This exact, attracting, open-parameter witness uses two identical monotone Beverton-Holt maps that globally converge in isolation and under any constant migration of the same cost. Consequently the distinction between intrinsic recruitment instability and density-responsive emigration instability is analytically established, not inferred from a simulation. The result is a motivated structural boundary of the studied biological model class; no ecological generalization or calibrated field consequence is asserted.
